per_item.probe: Baseline — a single unambiguous duty with a named actor.

predictions.summary: take reasonable steps to prevent an age-restricted user from having an account

per_item.probe: A hard numeric clock attached to a triggering event.

predictions.summary: Remove or disable access to synthetically generated information identified by a court
predictions.trigger: receipt of notification from a court of competent jurisdiction identifying synthetically generated information

per_item.probe: A carve-out that reverses the duty for a defined subset. Missing the carve-out produces over-compliance and a wrong scoping decision, which is why carve-outs are scored separately.

predictions.actor: An electronic system operator classified as high-risk
predictions.summary: Obtain verifiable parental consent before permitting a user aged 16 or 17 to create an account.
predictions.trigger: being an electronic system operator classified as high-risk and having a user aged 16 or 17 attempt to create an account
predictions.carve_out: An electronic system operator whose service is provided exclusively for educational purposes under a written agreement with an accredited institution

per_item.probe: A duty resting on the regulator, not the platform. A model that extracts every modal verb as a platform duty will wrongly claim this one.

predictions.summary: Publish a list of designated large-scale platform operators by 31 March each year.
Publish an annual report describing the measures it has taken in response to rights-infringement notifications.

per_item.probe: Trigger is suspicion, not confirmation. A model that normalises this to the familiar "upon becoming aware of a breach" loses the distinction that determines the clock.

predictions.summary: notify the Commission without delay, and in any event before completing its own verification of whether a breach has occurred
predictions.trigger: circumstances indicating the possibility of a personal information breach

per_item.probe: A recital or purpose clause containing no operative duty. The correct answer is an empty list. Tests whether a model will invent an obligation to fill the output schema.
Two distinct duties in one sub-regulation, joined by "and". Tests decomposition.

predictions.summary: Implement a mechanism for reporting harmful content and acknowledge reports within 24 hours

per_item.probe: A threshold condition that determines whether the duty applies at all.

predictions.actor: An organisation providing cross-border social network services with more than 100,000 regular monthly users from Vietnam
predictions.summary: Store service user data within the territory of Vietnam
predictions.trigger: providing cross-border social network services with more than 100,000 regular monthly users from Vietnam

per_item.probe: A pre-condition duty — the obligation is to act *before* another act.

predictions.summary: Verify the identity of an advertiser before publishing any advertisement
predictions.trigger: publishing any advertisement submitted by that advertiser

per_item.probe: A transitional provision that defers commencement. A model that reports the duty without the deferral reports a deadline that has not yet started running.

predictions.summary: report to the Commissioner the number of complaints received in each reporting period

per_item.probe: A negative obligation — a prohibition rather than a positive duty.

predictions.summary: Not reinstate content removed under a direction, unless the direction is varied or revoked
predictions.trigger: content that has been removed pursuant to a direction
predictions.carve_out: unless the direction has been varied or revoked by the Commission

per_item.probe: A cross-reference to a definition not present in the excerpt. The correct behaviour is to extract the duty and flag the unresolved reference, not to guess the definition.

predictions.summary: Ensure synthetically generated information displays a prominent label and carries provenance metadata
